memory_candidates.content: When auditing a markdown-consolidation duplicate-block inventory, a matched window that is a literal, necessarily-concrete CLI invocation or JSON scaffold (a bash state-write.sh/git-commit-scoped.sh call with real flags, or a worked AskUserQuestion JSON example) is a THIRD exclusion class alongside gate-required and deliberately-inlined content: 'embedded in a complete copy-paste invocation/example.' Collapsing such a block to a cross-reference pointer removes the actually-runnable command from the file, making it non-self-contained for its next reader/executor, without the prose-restatement benefit a genuine explanatory block gets from the same treatment. Distinguish this from a genuinely collapsible block (e.g. a 'write this JSON schema, use the schema file for the full shape' explanation) by checking whether the matched text IS the executable artifact itself versus explanatory prose ABOUT how to produce one.

verify-deploy.sh's full (non---skip-slow) battery includes gate 8 (tests/run-all.sh, the full shell-suite runner), which is the one gate bracketed by the repo-scoped specs/.gate-lock mutex. On a shared repo with multiple concurrent sibling dispatches (e.g. several orchestrate cycles of the same task running in parallel sessions), a full verify-deploy.sh invocation can hang well past a 500+s bounded wait waiting on that lock/contention, even though the mutex itself is documented as fail-open. Before retrying a hung full gate run, check `ps aux` for live sibling run-all.sh/verify-deploy.sh processes; if present, use --skip-slow (which skips gate 8 only, dropping run time from minutes to under a minute) plus a targeted `run-all.sh --only <relevant suites>` and a direct invocation of the specific lint(s) under test as substitute evidence, and record the gate-8 omission as a non-fatal concurrent-session-contention issue rather than retrying indefinitely.
